_meta.indication: TUKYSA in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine for treatment of adult patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, who have received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, active-comparator global trial; tucatinib 300 mg or placebo PO BID in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine, 21-day cycles.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, including those with brain metastases, who had received prior trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and T-DM1.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS) per BICR, analyzed in the ITT-PFS population (first 480 randomized subjects).
pivotal_trials.n: 612 randomized (410 tucatinib arm, 202 control arm); primary PFS analyzed in first 480.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nausea, fatigue, hepatotoxicity, vomiting, stomatitis. Diarrhea occurred in 81% (12% Grade 3, 0.5% Grade 4). Serious adverse reactions in 26%; fatal adverse reactions in 2%; discontinuation for AEs in 6%.
target_moa: Tucatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor of HER2; in vitro it inhibits phosphorylation of HER2 and HER3, inhibiting downstream MAPK and AKT signaling and cell proliferation, with reduced potency for related kinases (28- to 88-fold more potent for HER2 than EGFR).

rems.type: There is no indication for REMS.

companion_dx_detail: The applicant did not propose the use of a companion diagnostic or an FDA-approved test to select patients with HER2+ breast cancer.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class or in the intended population, and outside expertise was not necessary.

description.text: Added accelerated approval for tucatinib in combination with trastuzumab for RAS wild-type, HER2-positive, unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application adds a new indication of TUKYSA in combination with trastuzumab for the treatment of adult patients with RAS wild-type, HER2-positive, unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer that has progressed following treatment with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy.

basis.text: On December 16, 2019, FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to tucatinib in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine for locally advanced unresectable or metastatic breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, who received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting.

summary.text: TUKYSA received a regular (full) approval under 21 CFR 314.126 based on the single randomized HER2CLIMB trial. The NDA was a Priority review and was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation; it was reviewed under the Real-Time Oncology Review pilot and Project Orbis. It was not referred to an advisory committee.
